## 🔧 MASTER PROMPT FOR CLAUDE

You are working directly **inside my existing Replit repo** for VictorySync.
**Do not edit** `.replit` or `replit.nix`. Preserve all implemented features.
Make only the changes specified below. Commit in small, labeled chunks.

### GOALS

1. **Routing works everywhere**: clicking any nav item or button should navigate immediately (no “URL changes only” issue). Both **dev and prod** builds must render client routes (SPA fallback).
2. **Forgot Password** flows:

   * Customers: `/forgot-password` → email link → `/reset-password/:token`
   * Admins: `/admin/forgot-password` → email link → `/admin/reset-password/:token`
   * Dev mode: print reset links in server logs (no email provider required).
3. **Admin login query** uses the actual schema (no “failed query” banner).
4. **Hero section** uses the **VictorySync gradient + image** exactly like the deployed site.
5. Do **not** alter my public Nav / layout styling beyond the minimum to enable routing (convert `<a>` to `<Link>`). Match current look.

### STEP 1 — Fix SPA routing (React Router + fallback)

#### 1.1 Ensure `client/src/main.tsx` mounts a `BrowserRouter`

**File:** `client/src/main.tsx`
**Replace entire contents** with:

```tsx
import React from "react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
import { BrowserRouter } from "react-router-dom";
import App from "./App";

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <BrowserRouter>
      <App />
    </BrowserRouter>
  </React.StrictMode>
);
```

#### 1.2 Centralize routes

**File:** `client/src/App.tsx`
**Replace entire contents** with:

```tsx
import { Routes, Route, Navigate } from "react-router-dom";
import Home from "@/pages/Home";
import Login from "@/pages/auth/Login";
import Register from "@/pages/auth/Register";
import ForgotPassword from "@/pages/auth/ForgotPassword";
import ResetPassword from "@/pages/auth/ResetPassword";
import AdminLogin from "@/pages/admin/AdminLogin";
import AdminForgotPassword from "@/pages/admin/AdminForgotPassword";
import AdminResetPassword from "@/pages/admin/AdminResetPassword";
import About from "@/pages/About";
import Pricing from "@/pages/Pricing";
import Services from "@/pages/Services";
import Layout from "@/components/Layout";

// If your alias "@" isn't set, change imports to relative paths.

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Layout>
      <Routes>
        <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
        <Route path="/pricing" element={<Pricing />} />
        <Route path="/services" element={<Services />} />
        <Route path="/about" element={<About />} />

        {/* Customer auth */}
        <Route path="/login" element={<Login />} />
        <Route path="/register" element={<Register />} />
        <Route path="/forgot-password" element={<ForgotPassword />} />
        <Route path="/reset-password/:token" element={<ResetPassword />} />

        {/* Admin auth */}
        <Route path="/admin/login" element={<AdminLogin />} />
        <Route path="/admin/forgot-password" element={<AdminForgotPassword />} />
        <Route path="/admin/reset-password/:token" element={<AdminResetPassword />} />

        {/* Fallback */}
        <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} />
      </Routes>
    </Layout>
  );
}
```

#### 1.3 Convert header/footer nav `<a>` to React Router `<Link>`

**Files:** whatever contains public nav/footer (e.g., `client/src/components/Header.tsx`, `client/src/components/Footer.tsx`).
**Change examples:**

```tsx
// Before:
<a href="/pricing">Pricing</a>

// After:
import { Link } from "react-router-dom";
<Link to="/pricing">Pricing</Link>
```

For any **buttons** that navigate (e.g., “Sign In”, “Schedule Demo”, “View Pricing”), replace raw anchors with `<Link to="...">` or add `onClick={() => navigate("/path")}` using `useNavigate()`.

#### 1.4 Express SPA fallback (server)

**File:** `server/index.ts` — keep your API routes intact, add SPA fallback last.

Add **at the very bottom** (after all `/api` routes and static serving):

```ts
import path from "path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";
const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
const __dirname = path.dirname(__filename);

// Serve client build
const distDir = path.resolve(__dirname, "../client/dist");

app.use((req, res, next) => {
  if (req.path.startsWith("/api")) return next();
  // Always serve index.html for non-API routes
  res.sendFile(path.join(distDir, "index.html"));
});
```

> Do not remove any existing API; just ensure **non-/api** routes always get `index.html`.

### STEP 2 — Forgot Password (customers + admins)

#### 2.1 DB: password reset tokens

If using Drizzle or SQL, create a migration:

**File:** `server/db/migrations/xxxx_add_password_resets.ts`

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
export async function up(db: any) {
  await db.execute(sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS password_resets (
      id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
      user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      token_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
      role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('customer','admin')),
      created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
      used_at TIMESTAMP
    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_password_resets_token_hash ON password_resets(token_hash);
  `);
}
export async function down(db: any) {
  await db.execute(sql`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS password_resets;`);
}
```

Run your normal migration runner (whatever your repo uses).
If you don’t have a runner, keep this file and **Claude**, run it the same way other migrations are run in this codebase.

#### 2.2 Server routes

**File:** `server/routes/auth.reset.ts` (create)

```ts
import { Router } from "express";
import { z } from "zod";
import bcrypt from "bcryptjs";
import argon2 from "argon2";
import { db } from "../db"; // adapt import
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";

const r = Router();

const forgotSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
  role: z.enum(["customer","admin"]),
});

const resetSchema = z.object({
  token: z.string().min(10),
  password: z.string().min(8),
  role: z.enum(["customer","admin"]),
});

function devLogResetLink(link: string) {
  console.log("🔐 Password reset link:", link);
}

r.post("/auth/forgot", async (req, res) => {
  const parse = forgotSchema.safeParse(req.body);
  if (!parse.success) return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid" });
  const { email, role } = parse.data;

  // Look up user (adjust table/columns to match yours)
  const user = await db.oneOrNone(sql`
    SELECT id,email FROM users WHERE email = ${email} AND role = ${role === "admin" ? "admin" : "customer"}
  `);
  // Respond 200 even if not found (privacy)
  if (!user) return res.json({ ok: true });

  const raw = `${user.id}.${Date.now()}.${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;
  const tokenHash = await bcrypt.hash(raw, 10);
  await db.none(sql`
    INSERT INTO password_resets (user_id, token_hash, role)
    VALUES (${user.id}, ${tokenHash}, ${role})
  `);

  const token = Buffer.from(raw).toString("base64url");
  const base = process.env.PUBLIC_URL || ""; // if set; else blank
  const link = role === "admin"
    ? `${base}/admin/reset-password/${token}`
    : `${base}/reset-password/${token}`;

  // Dev: Show in logs
  devLogResetLink(link);

  // If you have an email provider, send mail here.

  res.json({ ok: true });
});

r.post("/auth/reset", async (req, res) => {
  const parse = resetSchema.safeParse(req.body);
  if (!parse.success) return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid" });
  const { token, password, role } = parse.data;

  let raw: string;
  try {
    raw = Buffer.from(token, "base64url").toString();
  } catch {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid token" });
  }

  const userIdStr = raw.split(".")[0];
  const userId = Number(userIdStr);
  if (!userId) return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid token" });

  // Validate token (fetch most recent unused token for user+role)
  const pr = await db.oneOrNone(sql`
    SELECT id, token_hash, used_at, created_at
    FROM password_resets
    WHERE user_id = ${userId} AND role = ${role}
    ORDER BY created_at DESC
    LIMIT 1
  `);
  if (!pr || pr.used_at) return res.status(400).json({ error: "Token expired" });
  const ok = await bcrypt.compare(raw, pr.token_hash);
  if (!ok) return res.status(400).json({ error: "Bad token" });

  const hash = await argon2.hash(password);
  await db.tx(async (t: any) => {
    await t.none(sql`UPDATE users SET password_hash = ${hash} WHERE id = ${userId}`);
    await t.none(sql`UPDATE password_resets SET used_at = NOW() WHERE id = ${pr.id}`);
  });

  res.json({ ok: true });
});

export default r;
```

**Wire these routes** in `server/routes.ts` (or wherever you combine routers):

```ts
import authReset from "./routes/auth.reset";
app.use("/api", authReset);
```

#### 2.3 Client pages (minimal, styled like your current forms)

Create these simple pages if they don’t exist:

**`client/src/pages/auth/ForgotPassword.tsx`**

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";

export default function ForgotPassword() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [sent, setSent] = useState(false);

  async function submit(e: React.FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault();
    await fetch("/api/auth/forgot", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ email, role: "customer" }),
    });
    setSent(true);
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-10 max-w-md mx-auto">
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-semibold mb-4">Forgot your password?</h1>
      {sent ? (
        <p>Check your email (or console logs in dev) for the reset link.</p>
      ) : (
        <form onSubmit={submit} className="space-y-4">
          <input
            className="input"
            placeholder="Your email"
            value={email}
            onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
          />
          <button className="btn btn-primary w-full">Send reset link</button>
        </form>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

**`client/src/pages/auth/ResetPassword.tsx`**

```tsx
import { useParams, useNavigate } from "react-router-dom";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function ResetPassword() {
  const { token } = useParams();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [ok, setOk] = useState(false);

  async function submit(e: React.FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault();
    const res = await fetch("/api/auth/reset", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ token, password, role: "customer" }),
    });
    if (res.ok) { setOk(true); setTimeout(()=>navigate("/login"), 1200); }
  }

  return (
    <div className="container py-10 max-w-md mx-auto">
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-semibold mb-4">Set a new password</h1>
      {ok ? <p>Password updated. Redirecting…</p> : (
        <form onSubmit={submit} className="space-y-4">
          <input
            className="input"
            type="password"
            placeholder="New password"
            value={password}
            onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
          />
          <button className="btn btn-primary w-full">Update password</button>
        </form>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

**Admin variants** (identical but role `"admin"` and routes under `/admin/...`):

**`client/src/pages/admin/AdminForgotPassword.tsx`** and
**`client/src/pages/admin/AdminResetPassword.tsx`** — copy the two components above, change `role: "customer"` → `role: "admin"` and redirect to `/admin/login`.

Add “Forgot password?” links:

* On customer login page → link to `/forgot-password`

### STEP 3 — Fix Admin login query to match schema

Where you verify admin credentials (e.g., `server/routes/auth.login.ts`), ensure the **exact** columns exist. Replace your SELECT with this safe form:

```ts
const admin = await db.oneOrNone(sql`
  SELECT id, email, password_hash, full_name, phone, org_id, role, permissions, mfa_enabled, created_at
  FROM users
  WHERE email = ${email} AND role = 'admin'
`);
```

Then verify password:

```ts
import argon2 from "argon2";
if (!admin) return res.status(401).json({ error: "Invalid credentials" });
const ok = await argon2.verify(admin.password_hash, password);
if (!ok) return res.status(401).json({ error: "Invalid credentials" });
```

> If your table/column names differ (e.g., `organization_id`), update the SELECT and the downstream code accordingly. The previous error on the admin login screen came from **selecting a column that doesn’t exist**—this fixes it.
